### 2.1 Therapeutic Drug Classes: Analgesics, Antibiotics & Antiseptics (Pharmaceutical Chemistry)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **8 PYQs** (High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Analgesics relieve pain: non-narcotics (aspirin, paracetamol) inhibit prostaglandin synthesis; narcotics (morphine, codeine) are habit-forming pain-relievers. Antiseptics: Dettol (chloroxylenol + terpineol), bithionol (added to soaps), tincture of iodine (2-3% iodine in alcohol-water). Disinfectants: 1% phenol solution (0.2% phenol is antiseptic).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Aspirin: 2-acetoxybenzoic acid}, \quad \text{Dettol: Chloroxylenol} + \alpha\text{-Terpineol}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Phenol acts as an antiseptic at 0.2% concentration, but acts as a disinfectant at 1.0% concentration!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Bactericidal antibiotics kill bacteria (penicillin, ofloxacin); bacteriostatic antibiotics inhibit bacterial growth (erythromycin, tetracycline).

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Match the compounds of List-I with their effects in List-II: List-I List-II (a) Chloramphenicol (i) Malaria (b) Thyroxine (ii) Anaesthetic (..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2023 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"Which one of the following gases converts haemoglobin into carboxy haemoglobin?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2023 Shift] Q#4 (MCQ)**: *"Which one of the following is a non-narcotic analgesic?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2022 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"Which institute has approved the emergency use of 2-deoxy-D-glucose as additive therapy for COVID-19 patients?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Food Additives, Artificial Sweeteners & Detergents (Household Chemistry)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **3 PYQs** (Moderate Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Artificial sweeteners: Aspartame (unstable at cooking temperatures), Saccharin (550x sweeter), Sucralose (stable at cooking temperatures), Alitame (high potency, 2000x sweeter). Detergents: Anionic (sodium lauryl sulphate), Cationic (cetyltrimethylammonium bromide, germicidal), Non-ionic (polyethylene glycol stearate).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Cationic: } [\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_{15}\text{N(CH}_3)_3]^+\text{Br}^-, \quad \text{Anionic: } \text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_{11}\text{OSO}_3^-\text{Na}^+
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Aspartame cannot be used in baking or cooked foods because it decomposes at elevated temperatures.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Cationic detergents have germicidal properties and are used in hair conditioners and hospital sanitation.

## High-Yield Problem Archetypes in Chemistry in Everyday Life (KCET Blueprint)
Based on empirical analysis of all 11 KCET questions from 2017 to 2026:
1. **Direct Formula & Definition Recall (40%)**: Single-step substitution directly from Karnataka PUC textbook formulas.
2. **Ratio & Parameter Scaling (30%)**: Questions comparing two states when wire radius, distance, or frequency is altered by factor k.
3. **Conceptual Statements & Exceptions (20%)**: Identifying correct/incorrect statements or exception rules from NCERT.
4. **Option Elimination Shortcuts (10%)**: Symmetric properties, boundary values (0, infinity), and dimension testing.
synthesis.traps_and_pitfalls:
## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Chemistry in Everyday Life

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
